ingredients.name: All-purpose flour
ingredients.notes: for the crepe batter; about 1 cup

ingredients.name: Eggs
ingredients.notes: 1 for the crepe batter, 1 beaten for coating the rolls

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: 1 cup; for the crepe batter -- some recipes use milk for a softer crepe

ingredients.name: Canned tuna or mackerel
ingredients.notes: 1 can; drained and flaked, large bones and dark skin removed

ingredients.name: Potato
ingredients.notes: boiled and mashed; helps bind the filling

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.notes: freshly ground; a generous amount is important

ingredients.name: Oil for deep frying
ingredients.notes: heat to 165-175C; low-medium heat prevents rolls from bursting open

steps.instruction: Make the crepe batter: whisk together the flour, 1 egg, water, and a pinch of salt until smooth and lump-free. Rest for 10 minutes. The batter should be thinner than pancake batter.

Make the filling: heat a little oil in a pan. Saute the onion, garlic, and carrot for 3 minutes until soft. Add the green chillies, curry leaves, chilli powder, and black pepper. Stir for 1 minute. Add the canned fish and mashed potato. Mix thoroughly until cohesive. Add lime juice and salt to taste. The filling should be dry -- a wet filling causes rolls to burst open. Cool completely.

Cook the crepes: heat a small non-stick pan over medium heat, lightly greased. Pour a small ladle of batter, swirl to coat the pan in a very thin even layer, and cook for about 1 minute until just set on top and lightly coloured on the bottom -- do NOT brown it or it will crack when rolled. Slide onto a plate. Repeat to make 12-15 thin crepes. Use the leftover batter for coating the rolls.

To roll: place a crepe on a flat surface. Add about 2-3 tablespoons of the cooled filling towards one end. Fold the two side edges inward over the filling, then roll firmly from the filling end to form a tight cylindrical shape. Dab a little leftover crepe batter on the final edge to seal. Roll tightly -- air gaps cause rolls to burst open during frying.
Coat each roll: dip in the remaining crepe batter (or beaten egg), let excess drip off, then roll in breadcrumbs pressing firmly all over. Refrigerate for 30 minutes to 1 hour to set the coating.

Heat oil to 165-175C (330-350F). Fry rolls in small batches for 4-6 minutes, turning gently, until deep golden brown all over. Medium heat is important -- too high heat causes rolls to burst. Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with tomato ketchup, chilli sauce, or a squeeze of lime.

source_site: hungrylankan.com, cross-checked against islandsmile.org, shanas.kitchen, ralahami.com, dailylife.lk, therecipe.website, theflavorbender.com, and cookpad.com
collection_method: scraped, cross-checked across 9+ independent sources; very strong agreement on three-component structure (crepe + spicy fish-potato filling + breadcrumb coating), rolling tightly to prevent bursting, and medium-heat frying
notes: Sri Lankan fish rolls (also called Chinese rolls or just 'rolls') are considered the most loved short eat alongside fish cutlets (sl_049) -- the difference being that rolls have a crepe wrapper while cutlets are plain breaded balls. Both share the same spiced fish-and-potato filling and the same anti-cracking/bursting rules: filling must be dry, rolling must be tight with no air gaps, and frying must be at medium rather than high heat. Three consistent failure modes across all sources: (1) filling too wet -> roll bursts; (2) crepe too thick or overcooked -> cracks when rolled; (3) oil too hot -> outside brown before inside heats through and roll may burst. The same crepe-and-breadcrumb technique works for chicken, beef, or vegetable fillings -- fish is most traditional.
